hook: I run Juniper Market. When an order arrived broken, I used to lose an afternoon to emails and photos. Now Refund Relay handles it.
setup1: Setting it up took me about five minutes. I made an account,
setup2: connected my own PayPal account, so refunds come straight from my store, not from a middleman,
setup3: and made a private key for my store's server.
plug1: Plugging it in is one step after checkout. My store tells Refund Relay about each paid order, and it checks that order with PayPal before accepting it.
plug2: Then every order page gets a Report a problem button.
rule1: Last, I told my refund agent, in plain English, what it may settle on its own.
rule2: It reads my rules back, with a daily limit, so there are no surprises.
store: Here's what my customers see. They pay with PayPal, like always.
chip1: A mug arrives chipped. They say what happened, add a photo, and send.
refunded: Moments later, twenty dollars is back in their PayPal. Nobody at my shop lifted a finger.
case: My case page shows why: the photo matched the mug we sold, the damage fit my rule, and PayPal confirmed the refund.
asst1: Customers who use their own assistant can file through it too.
vase1: A cracked vase is above my limit, so the agent hands it to me, already checked, with ideas: a repair kit, or something else in stock.
vase2: One click sends the choices, and the customer picks one. A refund just became the next sale.
wrong1: When a photo shows a different mug from the one we sold, nothing is paid.
wrong2: The agent holds it, and I ask for a photo of the label in one click.
log: I can see every decision the agent made, and why, and switch it off any time.
end: Refund Relay. Turn a broken order into the next sale.
